subject: Meridian Genomics Institute
text: Meridian Genomics Institute (MGI) is a gene therapy research center in Research Triangle Park, North Carolina, founded in 2028.

subject: Dr. Elena Vasquez
text: Dr. Elena Vasquez serves as Chief Scientific Officer at MGI, overseeing all research programs.

subject: Dr. Marcus Chen
text: Dr. Marcus Chen leads the gene therapy research division at MGI.

subject: Dr. Amara Obi
text: Dr. Amara Obi is Clinical Trial Director at MGI, responsible for all trial operations.

subject: Jordan Reeves
text: Jordan Reeves manages regulatory affairs at MGI, handling FDA submissions and compliance.

subject: MGT-401
text: MGT-401 is MGI's flagship gene therapy program targeting Duchenne muscular dystrophy (DMD).

subject: MGT-502
text: MGT-502 is a gene therapy program for spinal muscular atrophy (SMA) in active development at MGI.

subject: VP-3
text: Vector Platform VP-3 is an adeno-associated virus (AAV) delivery vector adopted by MGI for clinical use.

subject: Dr. Suki Tanaka
text: Dr. Suki Tanaka chairs the MGI Bioethics Committee.

subject: Dr. Felix Brennan
text: Dr. Felix Brennan is the toxicology specialist at MGI, responsible for safety assessments.

subject: MERIT-2
text: MERIT-2 was designed as a Phase III randomized controlled trial for MGT-401 in DMD patients aged 4-12.

subject: MERIT-2
text: MERIT-2 protocol received IRB approval on June 15, 2030.

subject: MERIT-2
text: Three clinical sites were selected for MERIT-2: Duke University Medical Center, Johns Hopkins, and Children's Hospital of Philadelphia.

subject: MERIT-2
text: The approved budget for MERIT-2 was $34.2 million over 3 years.

subject: MERIT-2
text: MERIT-2 launch was delayed when VP-3 manufacturing at the contract facility encountered yield problems, reducing available vector supply by 60%.

subject: MERIT-2
text: MERIT-2 was formally cancelled on March 8, 2031, before any patient was enrolled. The cancellation was due to manufacturing delays and competing data from Genexis Corp making the primary endpoint outdated.

subject: MERIT-2
text: MERIT-2 never enrolled a single patient. Zero subjects received treatment under this protocol.

subject: VP-5
text: VP-5, a lipid nanoparticle delivery vector, was evaluated over 6 months as a potential alternative to VP-3 for MGT-401 delivery.

subject: VP-5
text: In cell culture tests, VP-5 showed 23% higher transfection efficiency compared to VP-3.

subject: VP-5
text: VP-5 caused significant inflammatory responses in the murine model, with elevated IL-6 and TNF-alpha levels 3x above baseline.

subject: VP-5
text: The Scientific Advisory Board voted 7-1 against adopting VP-5 due to inflammatory response concerns. VP-5 was never used in any patient or clinical trial.

subject: MGT-401
text: Pre-clinical data suggested potential hepatotoxicity risk for MGT-401 due to liver tropism of the AAV vector.

subject: MERIT-1
text: Weekly liver function panels were mandated for all MERIT-1 participants as a hepatotoxicity monitoring protocol.

subject: MERIT-1 liver panels
text: All 24 MERIT-1 participants completed weekly liver function panels over 12 months. Every result was within normal limits. Zero hepatotoxicity events were recorded.

subject: MERIT-1
text: The final MERIT-1 safety report confirmed zero cases of hepatotoxicity across all 24 participants and all monitoring timepoints.

subject: BLA for MGT-401
text: The Biologics License Application (BLA) for MGT-401 was drafted over 8 months, from January to August 2031.

subject: MGI
text: MGI held a Type B pre-submission meeting with FDA's Center for Biologics Evaluation and Research on September 12, 2031.

subject: FDA
text: At the pre-submission meeting, FDA expressed concern that 18-month follow-up data was insufficient. They recommended 3-year durability data before BLA submission.

subject: BLA for MGT-401
text: The BLA for MGT-401 was withdrawn before formal submission to FDA. The decision was made on October 3, 2031, to wait for 3-year follow-up data.

subject: BLA for MGT-401
text: The BLA for MGT-401 was never formally filed with FDA. It remains in draft status pending 3-year durability data.

subject: Dr. Marcus Chen
text: Dr. Marcus Chen proposed MGT-603, a gene therapy program for cystic fibrosis, in a formal proposal submitted April 2030.

subject: MGT-603
text: A feasibility study for MGT-603 concluded that the CFTR gene correction approach was technically viable using the VP-3 vector platform.

subject: Bioethics Committee
text: The Bioethics Committee raised concerns about the small target patient population for MGT-603 and potential informed consent challenges with pediatric CF patients.

subject: MGT-603
text: The MGI board voted not to proceed with MGT-603. Resources were redirected to MGT-401 Phase III preparation and MGT-502 development.

subject: MGT-603
text: MGT-603 never entered development. No IND was filed, no preclinical studies were initiated, and no patients were ever treated under this program.

subject: NOVA-1
text: NOVA-1 was initiated as a Phase I dose-escalation trial for MGT-710, a CRISPR-based sickle cell treatment, enrolling 8 patients.

subject: NOVA-1
text: Three of the first 8 NOVA-1 patients developed immune reactions: elevated CRP, fever, and joint pain. These were immune-mediated, NOT hepatotoxicity.

subject: DSMB
text: The Data Safety Monitoring Board recommended pausing NOVA-1 enrollment after reviewing the 3 adverse events.

subject: NOVA-1
text: NOVA-1 was terminated on November 22, 2030, following DSMB review. Only 3 patients had received treatment; the remaining 5 enrolled patients did NOT receive the investigational product.

subject: NOVA-1
text: NOVA-1 did not complete its planned enrollment of 24 patients. Only 8 were enrolled and only 3 received treatment.

subject: Dr. Elena Vasquez
text: Dr. Vasquez authored a speculative whitepaper proposing combining MGT-401 with the small-molecule chaperone compound TRX-88 to enhance protein folding.

subject: Dr. Ravi Patel
text: Dr. Patel ran computational molecular dynamics simulations of the MGT-401 + TRX-88 combination, modeling protein-chaperone interactions over 500 nanoseconds.

subject: simulations
text: In silico simulations showed a predicted 35% improvement in dystrophin protein stability when co-administered with TRX-88. These results are computational only — no in vitro or in vivo testing was performed.

subject: MGT-401 + TRX-88 combination
text: The MGT-401 + TRX-88 combination therapy has never been tested in cell cultures, animal models, or human subjects. All results are from computational simulations only.

subject: Priya Sharma
text: Priya Sharma is the Data Analytics Lead at MGI, responsible for biostatistics and trial data analysis.

subject: Dr. Ravi Patel
text: Dr. Ravi Patel heads the computational biology division at MGI.

subject: Morgan Hale
text: Morgan Hale manages quality assurance at MGI, overseeing GMP compliance.

subject: Lisa Cartwright
text: Lisa Cartwright serves as Patient Advocacy Director at MGI.

subject: MERIT-1
text: MERIT-1 was the Phase II clinical trial for MGT-401, enrolling 24 DMD patients aged 6-14.

subject: MERIT-1
text: MERIT-1 demonstrated statistically significant improvement in the 6-minute walk test (mean +38 meters, p<0.01) at 12 months.

subject: MGT-710
text: MGT-710 uses CRISPR-Cas9 gene editing to correct the sickle cell mutation in HBB gene.

subject: MERIT-2
text: MERIT-2's primary endpoint was a 2-point improvement on the North Star Ambulatory Assessment at 18 months.

subject: MERIT-2
text: MERIT-2 planned to enroll 120 patients across 3 sites, randomized 2:1 treatment to placebo.

subject: Genexis Corp
text: Genexis Corp published Phase II data showing their GNX-201 achieved a 2.3-point NSAA improvement, making MERIT-2's chosen endpoint potentially outdated.

subject: MERIT-2 budget
text: After MERIT-2 cancellation, $18 million of the $34.2M budget was reallocated to accelerate MGT-502 SMA program development.

subject: VP-5
text: VP-5 was developed by NanoVec Therapeutics and licensed to MGI for evaluation as a delivery vector.

subject: VP-5
text: In biodistribution studies, VP-5 showed 4x higher liver accumulation than VP-3, raising hepatotoxicity concerns.

subject: Dr. Marcus Chen
text: Dr. Chen was the sole dissenting voice on the advisory board, arguing VP-5's efficiency advantages outweighed the inflammatory risk.

subject: VP-5 license
text: Following the rejection decision, MGI returned the VP-5 license to NanoVec Therapeutics in November 2029.

subject: hepatotoxicity risk
text: The hepatotoxicity concern for MGT-401 was based on published literature showing AAV8 liver toxicity in high-dose NHP studies.

subject: MERIT-1
text: MERIT-1 used doses 10x below the threshold associated with hepatotoxicity in NHP studies, which may explain the clean safety profile.

subject: Dr. Felix Brennan
text: Despite clean MERIT-1 results, Dr. Brennan recommended continuing hepatotoxicity monitoring in all future MGT-401 trials as a precautionary measure.

subject: BLA for MGT-401
text: The draft BLA for MGT-401 contained completed sections on chemistry, manufacturing, and controls (CMC), nonclinical studies, and clinical data from MERIT-1.

subject: FDA
text: During the pre-submission meeting, FDA acknowledged the MERIT-1 efficacy data was promising but insufficient alone for approval.

subject: revised BLA timeline
text: The revised BLA submission timeline targets Q2 2033, after 3-year MERIT-1 follow-up data is available.

subject: MGT-603 feasibility study
text: The MGT-603 feasibility study projected total program cost of $52 million over 5 years, including Phase I and Phase II trials.

subject: MGT-603
text: The MGT-603 proposal specified using the VP-3 AAV vector platform, modified for lung epithelial targeting.

subject: Lisa Cartwright
text: Lisa Cartwright advocated for MGT-603 before the board, citing unmet need in the CF patient community.

subject: NOVA-1 adverse events
text: The 3 NOVA-1 adverse events were classified as immune-mediated reactions to the CRISPR delivery complex, manifesting as elevated CRP, transient fever, and joint inflammation.

subject: NOVA-1 patients
text: All 3 NOVA-1 patients who experienced adverse events recovered fully within 2 weeks with corticosteroid treatment.

subject: MGT-710 program
text: Following NOVA-1 termination, the MGT-710 program was suspended pending development of a less immunogenic CRISPR delivery system.

subject: 5 enrolled NOVA-1 patients
text: The 5 enrolled but untreated NOVA-1 patients were offered referrals to competing sickle cell treatment trials.

subject: TRX-88
text: TRX-88 is a small-molecule protein chaperone developed at MIT, shown to stabilize misfolded proteins in neurodegenerative disease models.

subject: Vasquez whitepaper
text: Dr. Vasquez presented the combination therapy whitepaper at the Q3 2031 science meeting. It was received as an interesting theoretical direction but no action items were assigned.

subject: Dr. Ravi Patel
text: Dr. Patel explicitly cautioned that in silico results cannot predict in vivo outcomes and recommended in vitro validation before any clinical consideration.

subject: MGI
text: As of 2032, MGI has two active therapeutic programs: MGT-401 for DMD and MGT-502 for SMA. MGT-603 was never started and MGT-710 is suspended.

subject: MGI
text: As of 2032, MERIT-1 is the only clinical trial MGI has completed. MERIT-2 was cancelled before launch and NOVA-1 was terminated early.

subject: MGI annual review 2031
text: The 2031 annual review noted MGI completed MERIT-1 successfully but faced setbacks: MERIT-2 cancelled, NOVA-1 terminated, BLA withdrawn, and MGT-603 not approved.

subject: MERIT-2 protocol
text: MERIT-2 protocol specified a 24-month treatment period with 12 months of post-treatment follow-up.

subject: MERIT-2
text: MERIT-2 planned to use VP-3 vector at 1.5x the dose used in MERIT-1, based on dose-response modeling.

subject: Duke site coordinator
text: The Duke site completed staff training and facility preparation for MERIT-2 before learning of the cancellation.

subject: MERIT-2 patient screening
text: Patient screening for MERIT-2 never began at any of the three selected clinical sites.

subject: VP-5 first evaluation report
text: The first VP-5 evaluation report showed promising transfection results in HEK293 and myoblast cell lines, with 23% improvement over VP-3.

subject: VP-5 second evaluation
text: The second VP-5 evaluation report revealed dose-dependent immunogenicity in the murine model, with anti-PEG antibodies detected in 60% of animals.

subject: VP-5
text: VP-5 evaluation was halted before non-human primate studies. All data is from murine models and cell culture only.

subject: MERIT-1 patient 007
text: MERIT-1 patient 007 showed mildly elevated ALT at week 4 (42 U/L, upper normal 45 U/L). This was within normal limits and resolved spontaneously.

subject: MERIT-1 DSMB
text: The MERIT-1 DSMB reviewed all liver function data at interim analysis and found no safety signal. They recommended continuing without protocol modification.

subject: hepatotoxicity risk
text: Following MERIT-1 clean safety data, the hepatotoxicity risk for MGT-401 was downgraded from 'moderate' to 'low probability' in the risk register.

subject: BLA CMC section
text: Morgan Hale led the completion of the Chemistry, Manufacturing, and Controls section of the MGT-401 BLA.

subject: BLA clinical section
text: Priya Sharma compiled the clinical data section of the BLA, including all MERIT-1 efficacy and safety results.

subject: pre-submission FDA meeting
text: The Type B pre-submission meeting with FDA was attended by Jordan Reeves, Dr. Vasquez, and Dr. Obi from MGI.

subject: FDA reviewer
text: The FDA reviewer also requested additional immunogenicity data for the anti-AAV antibody response in the BLA.

subject: MGT-603
text: MGT-603 proposed full-length CFTR gene replacement using a dual-vector AAV approach, a technically ambitious strategy.

subject: Dr. Suki Tanaka
object: CF patient population is small but has high unmet need
text: Dr. Tanaka acknowledged the high unmet need in CF but noted that the target subpopulation (specific CFTR mutations) numbered fewer than 5,000 patients in the US.

subject: board vote on MGT-603
text: The board voted 6-2 against proceeding with MGT-603, with Dr. Chen and Lisa Cartwright dissenting.

subject: NOVA-1 dose level 1
text: The first 3 NOVA-1 patients received dose level 1 at 5e12 vector genomes per kilogram.

subject: NOVA-1 dose level 2
text: Dose level 2 (1e13 vg/kg) was never administered. The trial was terminated before dose escalation.

subject: NOVA-1 patient 004
text: NOVA-1 patient 004 experienced grade 2 fever (39.2°C) and joint pain beginning 48 hours post-infusion.

subject: NOVA-1 patients 001-003
text: NOVA-1 patients 001, 002, and 003 all received treatment at dose level 1. Patients 001-003 did not experience adverse events initially, but patients 004, 005, 006 (the next three in the cohort) had immune reactions. Only 3 of the first enrolled 8 were treated.

subject: Patel simulations
text: Dr. Patel's molecular dynamics simulations used the published dystrophin spectrin-like repeat crystal structure (PDB: 1DXX) as the starting conformation.

subject: TRX-88 binding affinity
text: Simulations predicted TRX-88 binding to dystrophin with an affinity of Kd = 2.3 nM, suggesting tight binding if confirmed experimentally.

subject: combination therapy proposal
text: The MGT-401 + TRX-88 combination therapy was not included in MGI's 2032-2035 strategic plan. It remains a theoretical concept only.

subject: MGI
text: MGI has proposed four gene therapy programs: MGT-401 (DMD, active), MGT-502 (SMA, active), MGT-603 (CF, never started), and MGT-710 (sickle cell, suspended).

subject: MGI
text: MGI evaluated two vector platforms: VP-3 (AAV, adopted and used in all trials) and VP-5 (lipid nanoparticle, rejected after evaluation).

subject: MGI regulatory submissions
text: As of 2032, MGI has made zero approved regulatory submissions. The sole BLA attempt for MGT-401 was withdrawn before formal filing.

subject: MERIT-2 enrollment criteria
object: ambulatory boys aged 4-12 with confirmed DMD
text: MERIT-2 would have enrolled ambulatory boys aged 4-12 with genetically confirmed DMD and NSAA score between 15 and 35.

subject: VP-5 evaluation cost
text: The total cost of the VP-5 evaluation program was $2.8 million over 6 months, covering cell culture, animal studies, and advisory board review.

subject: Dr. Brennan
text: Dr. Brennan testified to the MERIT-1 DSMB that after 12 months of weekly monitoring, there was no hepatotoxicity signal in any patient.

subject: Reeves
text: Jordan Reeves estimated that revising the BLA with 3-year data would cost an additional $3.5 million.

subject: MGT-710 reformulation
text: The reformulation of MGT-710's CRISPR delivery system to reduce immunogenicity is expected to take 18-24 months.

subject: TRX-88 developer
text: MGI has not contacted the TRX-88 developer at MIT about licensing or collaboration. The compound remains in academic research only.

subject: MERIT-2 statistician
text: Priya Sharma calculated that 120 patients (80:40 randomization) would provide 80% power to detect a 2-point NSAA improvement.

subject: CHOP site
text: Children's Hospital of Philadelphia completed all local regulatory and ethics approvals for MERIT-2 by July 2030.

subject: Johns Hopkins site
text: Johns Hopkins identified 32 potential MERIT-2 candidates from their DMD registry, but none were ever contacted for screening.

subject: VP-3 manufacturing yield
text: VP-3 manufacturing yield at the contract facility dropped to 40% of the target needed for MERIT-2 supply.

subject: VP-5 third evaluation
text: The third VP-5 report characterized dose-dependent inflammatory markers at 3 dose levels in mice, confirming a clear dose-toxicity relationship.

subject: advisory board meeting
text: The advisory board meeting on VP-5 lasted 4 hours. Dr. Chen argued for conditional adoption with dose optimization; the majority cited unacceptable risk.

subject: VP-5 evaluation data
text: VP-5 evaluation data was published in the Journal of Gene Medicine as a negative result, contributing to the scientific literature on lipid nanoparticle vector safety.

subject: AAV8 hepatotoxicity
text: Sparks et al. (2028) reported dose-dependent hepatotoxicity in NHP receiving AAV8 at doses above 1e14 vg/kg, the primary basis for MGT-401 risk assessment.

subject: MERIT-1 dose
text: MERIT-1 used MGT-401 at 1e13 vg/kg, a full order of magnitude below the 1e14 vg/kg threshold associated with hepatotoxicity in the Sparks NHP study.

subject: MERIT-1 liver monitoring
text: MERIT-1 liver monitoring included weekly ALT, AST, total bilirubin, and GGT panels for all 24 participants.

subject: no MERIT-1 patient
text: No MERIT-1 patient required dose modification, treatment delay, or early discontinuation due to liver function concerns.

subject: BLA nonclinical section
text: The nonclinical section of the draft BLA included data from 12 preclinical studies spanning biodistribution, toxicology, and pharmacology.

subject: BLA team
text: The MGI regulatory team logged approximately 8,400 person-hours on BLA preparation before the withdrawal decision.

subject: BLA withdrawal
text: Since the BLA was withdrawn before formal submission, there was no FDA penalty, refusal-to-file, or negative precedent for future MGT-401 submissions.

subject: MGT-603 dual-vector approach
text: The dual-vector AAV approach proposed for MGT-603 had not been previously tested in any CF model. It was a novel technical approach without proof-of-concept.

subject: existing CF therapies
text: The board noted that existing CF therapies (CFTR modulators) had already improved median survival to 56 years, reducing the urgency for gene therapy.

subject: MGT-603 IND
text: No IND (Investigational New Drug) application was ever filed for MGT-603. The program stopped at the proposal stage.

subject: NOVA-1 enrollment period
text: NOVA-1 enrolled 8 patients between January and March 2030.

subject: NOVA-1 treatment period
text: NOVA-1 treatment was administered to 3 patients between March and May 2030 before the DSMB pause.

subject: NOVA-1 informed consent
text: The NOVA-1 informed consent form listed immune reactions as a potential risk, based on preclinical CRISPR delivery data.

subject: NOVA-1 did_not_test
text: NOVA-1 was terminated before any efficacy assessment could be made. No efficacy data exists for MGT-710 in humans.

subject: Patel simulations
text: Dr. Patel's simulations ran for 720 hours on MGI's HPC cluster, consuming approximately $15,000 in compute resources.

subject: simulation
text: The Patel simulations modeled only protein-chaperone binding dynamics. They did not model immune response, toxicity, pharmacokinetics, or delivery.

subject: Dr. Vasquez
object: combination therapy is years away from testing
text: At the Q3 2031 meeting, Dr. Vasquez acknowledged that even if funded, combination therapy testing would require 2-3 years of preclinical work before any human trial.

subject: MGI safety record
object: no serious treatment-related adverse events in DMD trials
text: MGI's safety record shows no serious treatment-related adverse events in its DMD program. MERIT-1 had a clean safety profile.

subject: MGI annual budget
text: MGI's total annual operating budget is approximately $85 million, split between research, clinical operations, and manufacturing.

subject: MGI
text: MGI employs approximately 340 staff across research, clinical, regulatory, and administrative divisions.

subject: MGI
object: UNC Chapel Hill for basic research
text: MGI maintains a research partnership with UNC Chapel Hill for basic gene therapy vector biology research.

subject: MGT-502 SMA program
text: As of 2032, MGT-502 is in late preclinical development, with an IND filing expected in Q1 2033.

subject: DMD
text: Duchenne muscular dystrophy affects approximately 1 in 3,600 male births worldwide.

subject: MERIT-1
text: MERIT-1 was conducted at a single site: Duke University Medical Center.

subject: MERIT-1
text: MERIT-1 enrolled 24 DMD patients between June 2029 and January 2030.

subject: MERIT-2 CRO
text: Parexel International was contracted as the CRO for MERIT-2. The contract was terminated with a $1.2M penalty after cancellation.

subject: MERIT-2 Data Management Plan
text: Priya Sharma finalized the MERIT-2 data management plan, including eCRF design and statistical analysis plan, none of which were ever used.

subject: MERIT-2 cancellation
object: approximately $32 million in direct trial costs
text: Cancelling MERIT-2 before enrollment saved MGI approximately $32 million in direct trial costs, though $2.1M had been spent on preparation.

subject: MERIT-2 comparator arm
text: MERIT-2 planned a placebo-controlled design with standard of care as the comparator arm.

subject: VP-3
object: sole vector platform after VP-5 rejection
text: After VP-5 rejection, VP-3 remained MGI's sole delivery vector platform. No other alternatives have been evaluated since.

subject: NanoVec Therapeutics
text: NanoVec Therapeutics subsequently reported successful use of VP-5 in an oncology application in 2031, suggesting the vector may be viable in different contexts.

subject: VP-5 inflammatory dose
text: The VP-5 inflammatory response was observed at doses of 1e12 particles/kg in mice, which would extrapolate to clinically relevant doses in humans.

subject: MERIT-1 patients
text: No liver biopsies were performed on MERIT-1 patients. Monitoring relied solely on blood-based liver function panels.

subject: liver monitoring costs
text: Weekly liver monitoring for all 24 MERIT-1 patients over 12 months cost approximately $180,000 in lab fees.

subject: AAV liver tropism
text: AAV liver tropism is well-documented in gene therapy literature, making hepatotoxicity monitoring standard practice for all AAV-based trials.

subject: BLA pre-submission package
text: The complete BLA pre-submission package totaled 2,300 pages across CMC, nonclinical, and clinical modules.

subject: FDA Type B meeting
text: The official outcome of the FDA Type B meeting was 'proceed with caution' — FDA did not reject the program but recommended additional data before filing.

subject: MGI board
text: The MGI board unanimously approved the BLA withdrawal decision, agreeing that premature submission risked a complete response letter.

subject: Dr. Chen
text: Dr. Chen expressed disappointment at the MGT-603 board decision, noting it represented 6 months of his research team's work.

subject: MGT-603 research materials
text: All MGT-603 proposal materials, feasibility data, and technical designs were archived in the MGI research library for potential future reference.

subject: CF gene therapy field
text: As of 2032, no company has received regulatory approval for a CF gene therapy, suggesting the field remains challenging.

subject: NOVA-1 site
text: NOVA-1 was conducted at MGI's own on-site clinical facility, not at an external academic medical center.

subject: MGT-710 IP
text: MGT-710 was developed under a CRISPR licensing agreement with the Broad Institute. The license remains active despite program suspension.

subject: NOVA-1 termination report
text: The NOVA-1 termination was reported to ClinicalTrials.gov with status 'Terminated' and reason 'Safety (immune-mediated adverse events).'

subject: NOVA-1 cost
text: NOVA-1 cost approximately $4.5 million before termination, including patient recruitment, treatment, and monitoring.

subject: TRX-88
object: 12 nM for protein stabilization in vitro
text: Published academic studies show TRX-88 has an IC50 of 12 nM for protein stabilization in cell-free assays.

subject: MGI
text: No budget was allocated for MGT-401 + TRX-88 combination therapy research in any fiscal year. The simulations used existing compute allocation.

subject: combination therapy concept
text: The MGT-401 + TRX-88 combination was assessed at Technology Readiness Level 2 — concept formulated but no experimental proof of concept.

subject: MGI GMP facility
text: MGI operates a GMP manufacturing facility for VP-3 vector production, with an annual capacity of 200 clinical doses.

subject: MGI
object: FDA Orphan Drug Designation for MGT-401
text: MGT-401 received FDA Orphan Drug Designation in 2029, providing regulatory advantages including tax credits and market exclusivity.

subject: MGI
object: Dr. Vasquez and Dr. Chen in 2028
text: MGI was co-founded by Dr. Elena Vasquez and Dr. Marcus Chen in 2028, backed by $150 million in Series A funding.

subject: MGI Series B funding
text: MGI raised $220 million in Series B funding in 2031, primarily to support MGT-401 Phase III development and MGT-502 IND preparation.

subject: MGI
object: VP-3 vector modifications and MGT-401 construct
text: MGI holds 14 patents related to VP-3 vector modifications and the MGT-401 gene therapy construct.

subject: MGI Scientific Advisory Board
text: MGI's Scientific Advisory Board consists of 7 external academic experts and 3 internal senior scientists.

subject: MGI
text: MGI is classified as a clinical-stage biotechnology company with one completed Phase II trial and no approved products.

subject: DMD gene therapy market
text: The global DMD gene therapy market is projected to reach $5.2 billion by 2035.

subject: MERIT-1 primary endpoint
text: MERIT-1 met its primary endpoint: statistically significant improvement in the 6-minute walk test at 12 months.

subject: MERIT-1 secondary endpoints
text: MERIT-1 secondary endpoints showed increased dystrophin protein levels in muscle biopsies (mean 28% of normal vs 3% at baseline).

subject: MGI Quality Management System
text: MGI's quality management system is certified to ISO 13485, covering design, development, and manufacturing of gene therapy products.

subject: MGI data infrastructure
text: MGI uses REDCap (Research Electronic Data Capture) for all clinical trial data management.

subject: MERIT-2
text: MERIT-2 has a final status of 'cancelled.' All planning artifacts (protocol, sites, budget) exist but no trial activities were ever executed.

subject: MGT-603
text: MGT-603 has a final status of 'rejected at proposal stage.' No development work was initiated beyond feasibility analysis.

subject: MGT-710
text: MGT-710 has a status of 'suspended pending reformulation.' No timeline for resumption has been set.

subject: BLA for MGT-401
text: The MGT-401 BLA has a status of 'withdrawn pending 3-year data.' Target resubmission is Q2 2033.

subject: MERIT-2 monitoring committee
text: The independent MERIT-2 monitoring committee was disbanded in April 2031 following trial cancellation.

subject: MERIT-2 investigator brochure
text: The MERIT-2 investigator brochure was completed in May 2030 but never distributed to clinical sites due to the subsequent cancellation.

subject: Genexis Corp GNX-201
text: Genexis Corp's competing DMD therapy GNX-201 entered Phase III in late 2030, making MERIT-2's original endpoint design less competitive.

subject: VP-3 manufacturing cost
text: VP-3 manufacturing cost is approximately $45,000 per clinical dose at MGI's GMP facility.

subject: VP-5 projected cost
text: VP-5 was projected to cost only $12,000 per dose if adopted, one-quarter of VP-3 manufacturing costs — a factor Dr. Chen cited in his dissent.

subject: post-MERIT-1 hepatotoxicity review
object: MGT-401 is safe at therapeutic doses
text: A comprehensive post-MERIT-1 hepatotoxicity review concluded that MGT-401 at therapeutic doses (1e13 vg/kg) poses negligible liver toxicity risk.

subject: MGT-401 hepatotoxicity risk
text: Hepatotoxicity was removed from the MGT-401 top-5 program risk register in 2032 following consistently clean safety data.

subject: BLA withdrawal
text: The BLA withdrawal decision was communicated to investors during MGI's Q4 2031 earnings call, along with the revised Q2 2033 timeline.

subject: Dr. Chen
text: After MGT-603 rejection, Dr. Chen redirected his CF-related lung delivery expertise to optimizing MGT-502's delivery to motor neurons.

subject: MGT-603 feasibility data
text: Some vector modification data from the MGT-603 feasibility study was later used to inform MGT-502's AAV capsid engineering.

subject: NOVA-1 adverse events
text: None of the 3 NOVA-1 adverse events were classified as life-threatening (CTCAE grade 4 or 5). All were grade 2.

subject: NOVA-1 data
text: MGI shared NOVA-1 safety data with two other CRISPR therapy developers under confidential data-sharing agreements to help the field learn from the adverse events.

subject: Dr. Patel
text: Dr. Patel published the simulation methodology and code on GitHub as an open-source contribution, though the specific TRX-88 binding data was kept proprietary.

subject: no patent application
text: No patent application was filed for the MGT-401 + TRX-88 combination concept. The idea remains unprotected IP.

subject: MGI
text: MGI maintains an independent Data Safety Monitoring Board for each active clinical trial, as required by FDA.

subject: MGI publication record
text: MGI researchers have published 23 peer-reviewed papers as of 2032, covering gene therapy vector biology, preclinical results, and MERIT-1 outcomes.

subject: MGI
text: As of 2032, MGI has no approved products on the market. It remains a clinical-stage company.

subject: MGI clinical operations team
text: MGI's clinical operations team consists of 28 staff members led by Dr. Amara Obi.

subject: MGI regulatory team
text: MGI's regulatory affairs team consists of 6 staff members led by Jordan Reeves.

subject: MERIT-1 safety data
text: The clean MERIT-1 safety data directly contradicts the pre-clinical expectation of hepatotoxicity risk for AAV-based gene therapies at therapeutic doses.

subject: NOVA-1 termination
text: The early termination of NOVA-1 contradicts the original plan to enroll 24 patients across multiple dose levels.

subject: MERIT-2 cancellation
text: The cancellation of MERIT-2 contradicts the previously approved $34.2M budget allocation, most of which was never spent.

subject: board rejection of MGT-603
text: The board rejection of MGT-603 contradicts the feasibility study that found the program technically viable.

subject: FDA durability concern
text: The FDA concern about insufficient long-term data contradicts MGI's belief that 18-month MERIT-1 efficacy data was adequate for BLA submission.

subject: absence of experimental evidence
text: The complete absence of experimental validation contradicts the promising in silico predictions for the MGT-401 + TRX-88 combination.
